market_holds: Spot $1.755 (sealed baseline 2026-11-13), 0.9% above the 52-week low and 58% below the high. It drifted from about $1.90 to $1.75 over three weeks while KWEB fell about 6% (Yahoo bars), so the run-in is mostly the China-ADR tape. There is no option chain (empty_chain), so nothing states an implied move. The baseline's 4.6% median reaction is contaminated by volume-update 6-Ks. Read off the bars, the true earnings-day reactions over the last year were -6.9% (2025-11-17: opened +6%, closed down), -14.7% (2026-03-16, with a further -8% the next day), -14.8% (2026-05-18) and -17.1% (2026-08-10, opened -14%). Coverage is two or three analysts. Stockanalysis shows a stale FY26 non-GAAP EPS of +1.28 (checked 2026-11-02) against a YTD net loss of RMB 196m, and an average target of $2.56. The Q2 call had no questions at all (auto transcript). Company Q3 guide (2026-08-10): RMB 1,863-2,033m, +10-20% YoY, with no margin guide. Q3 volume has been public since 2026-10-05: 537,457 units, +15.4% (China +9%, international +226%). The stock rose 3% that day and gave it back. Short interest is 0.5% of float, so no squeeze fuel. Turnover is about $190k a day. Net cash: the 2026-06-30 6-K shows RMB 1,476m of cash and investments plus RMB 218m restricted, against RMB 220m of borrowings. On roughly 75m ADS (my estimate from the short-interest share) the stock trades well below net cash.
view: I think this print is more likely to disappoint than not, on three lines the price has been punished for every time this year: revenue against the company's own guide, gross margin and a peak-quarter loss. Revenue first. Q3 volume of 537k units against my rebuild of revenue per unit gives RMB 1.74-1.88bn. China revenue per unit fell 9.2% in Q2 as e-motorcycles grew to about 60% of the mix, and peers cut prices RMB 400-800 around 618. International units tripled, but management called this a kick-scooter inventory clearance at low margin. Accessories grew about 29%. My central estimate is about RMB 1.81bn, below the RMB 1.863bn low end of the guide, which would be a second straight miss: Q2 came in at +14.7% against a +25-45% guide. China's +9% is only in line with the industry's Q3 (+9% YoY per AVC via 36Kr, 2026-11-09), so NIU is no longer taking share, and the Speed/e-motorcycle mix keeps pulling price per unit down. Margin next. Q2 gross margin was 16.0% (20.1% a year earlier) on mix, upstream costs and kick-scooter clearance, and all three were still active in Q3. Peers' profits are falling (Aima Q1-Q3 net -42%, Yadea H1 -27%). At about 16-19% gross margin on about RMB 1.8bn, against opex that ran RMB 297m in Q3 2025 and RMB 341m in Q2 2026, the seasonally strongest quarter lands near breakeven or at a loss. That compares with RMB 81.7m of profit a year ago, so the headline will read as a collapse. The FY26 volume target of 1.67-1.91m units would need about 450k+ in Q4 against 179k in Q4 2025, so the Q4 guide will in effect abandon it. The one upside route is the Q4 guide: Q4 2025 was depressed at RMB 676m, so a large YoY percentage is easy. But in March and May this year strong growth guides (+30-50%, +25-45%) still came with -15% days because the loss line led. Valuation below net cash has not cushioned any of the last three prints. The reaction sits at the open and the window runs to 13:00 ET, so it is captured.
unpriced: The Q3 revenue shortfall against the guide follows from public arithmetic (volume out since 2026-10-05, Q2 revenue per unit and segment mix in the 6-K), but nobody visibly does that arithmetic. Coverage is two or three analysts, the FY EPS consensus is a stale positive figure, and the last call had zero questions. The stock even rose on the volume release. With no implied move and no quantified preview, nothing shows that the price holds a second guide miss and a peak-quarter loss. The stock's level reflects general gloom, not this specific shortfall.

recommendation.reason: Rebuilding Q3 revenue from the published volume (537k units, China +9% in line with the industry) and Q2's falling price per unit, plus the kick-scooter clearance, puts revenue at about RMB 1.81bn, below the RMB 1.863-2.033bn guide. Gross margin is still squeezed by mix, upstream costs and clearance, so the peak quarter is near breakeven or a loss against RMB 81.7m of profit a year ago. Nobody visible prices this: two or three analysts, a stale positive EPS consensus, zero questions on the last call, and a stock that rose on the volume print. Each of the last four prints fell 7-17%, with the move largely at the open, which sits inside the 13:00 ET window.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 revenue at or above RMB 1.86bn with gross margin back near 19-20% and a Q3 net profit, especially if the call quantifies the higher-priced e-bike relaunch. A Q4 guide far above the 676m base, paired with a margin recovery statement, would also do it.

self_critique: The stock trades well below net cash at a 52-week low after four straight big earnings-day drops, so some of the bad news must be in it; extrapolating the last reactions is a known bias. China revenue per unit could recover in Q3 if the RMB 5,000-7,000 e-bike relaunch landed, which would put revenue at the guide (my high case is 1.88bn). An easy Q4 comparison could produce a large headline growth guide. In a $190k-a-day name, any surprise-free print could squeeze a few cents up. My revenue rebuild rests on assumed international and accessory revenue per unit. These keep me at 65, not higher.
approach_notes: P6 (find the line from past reactions) paid most: reading the bars myself showed the baseline's history was wrong for March, and the loss line led every drop. P3's own-arithmetic rebuild was the decisive source. P4 helped frame why a public volume number can still be unpriced in a name with no analyst questions.
